泡泡玛特创始人提出过一个很有意思的观点。

就算是千万富翁，出门忘记关掉水龙头照样会觉得心疼。一天仅仅浪费三十块，对富人来说算不上什么大钱，心里依旧会觉得别扭。但小区里的高级景观喷泉全天开启，一天消耗三百块，人们却完全不在意。

原因在于，水龙头流出的是实用水资源，会触发人的理性成本考量，三十块的损耗就会觉得昂贵;而喷泉的水没有实际用处，提供的是情绪与观赏体验，所以大家不会计较花销。

由此得出：情绪价值比实用价值更值钱。

text:
为什么前沿模型放出的成果几乎都是清一色的数学证明，物理定律的发现与突破等于0？

到现在为止，人类物理领域最后一次框架级事件是 1925–1926年的矩阵力学/波动力学。
如果宽松一点，我可以算到 1973年的渐近自由和标准模型闭合。之后的50年时间，物理学家数量涨了两个数量级，经费涨了三个，产出的框架级结果是 0。

如果人类以百倍的智力投入、半个世纪，也没做出来，那这件事的困难就不在认知端。
指望AI模型做到，等于指望它解决一个难度完全位于认知之外的问题。

数学的真理判据在问题内部；
物理的真理判据在世界外部。

数学特别适合当前 AI，是因为它近乎形成了一个完美的封闭环境。
给你 axioms、definitions、conjecture，然后模型搜索证明，最后一步甚至可以被 Lean、Isabelle、Coq的形式验证器机械判定。
于是，AI 可以做海量搜索、失败、反馈、再搜索。Reward 极其干净：proof checked = 1，proof failed = 0。
这恰好是强化学习、搜索、test-time compute 最喜欢的问题结构。

物理完全不是这样。
AI模型无论进化多少代，架构与训练网络不变，它就永远写不出牛顿三大定律和万有引力定律，我可以确信以及肯定这件事。
因为现代的LLM 极度偏向 interpolation，而基本物理革命往往要求 representation break。前者的训练目标要求它学习人类已有分布，所以产生一个真正脱离已有 ontology 的 representation，比在既有 representation 内做推理难得多。
即使它能写出类似的东西或定理，你无法在把它丢给一个“Physics Verifier”之后，机器告诉你 TRUE。
目前看来，一个基本物理假说可能要等 CERN、LIGO、JWST、量子实验室或者新的精密仪器给它一个数据点。
这造成了一个极其严重的feedback bandwidth mismatch。

假设今天把整个物理学文献、实验数据库、arXiv 都给 GPT-级模型，它会看到成千上万个 anomaly：
3 sigma deviation、材料中的反常行为、Hubble tension、muon anomaly、暗物质候选、超导异常、核结构问题……

最后的结果是，AI 越完美地学习现有物理学家的 priors，它越可能成为一个极其优秀的正常科学家。
但是，正常，意味着它永远无法做出范式突破。
目前的模型，无论Astra也好，还是没有彻底公开的Mythos，仍然生活在text、code、images和datasets里。
但是，自然科学家生活在world。
Faraday 可以不停摆弄线圈和磁铁，Rutherford 可以看散射数据，Michelson 可以重新设计光学装置。

实验科学中，有一个非常强大的能力叫intervention，拥有这种能力会每天问自己：如果我主动改变世界，会发生什么？
AI，没有操纵现实、改造实验的欲求。

这就是我们今天看到的趋势，AI 数学能力会先于 AI 基础物理发现能力十几年成熟。
Google DeepMind 的 AlphaEvolve 已经开始把能力扩展到模拟和科学问题，但其最漂亮的成果仍然集中在那些具有明确 objective function、可以高速计算验证的领域。
但距离物理定律级别的发现，AI还有太长的路。

text:
KTV经理收到一份“灭绝级”订台要求，看完第一句就懵了

一名男子加上KTV经理微信，上来先确认：

“您好，你是KTV经理吗？”

对方客客气气回复：

“哥您好，我是本店经理。”

男子立刻开始安排今晚的排面：

8个人左右，酒水预算1000。

等他到了以后，先叫2个保安到门口接，再安排6个美女站成两排，每人手里拿个礼炮。

然后送两支轩V，再来两箱啤酒。

最后还得把老板叫过来，亲自敬一杯酒。

男子把这一整套要求发完，还很自然地问：

“找你安排应该没问题吧？”

经理盯着手机沉默了几秒：

“您刚才说什么？🤔”

男子以为对方没看清，又重复了一句：

“晚上订个包。”

经理：

“不是这句，上一句。”

男子：

“您好，你是KTV经理吗？”

经理终于绷不住了：

“我不是😭”

估计干KTV这么多年，也是第一次遇到有人拿1000块酒水预算，想体验一把“集团董事长秘密视察分公司”的待遇。

text:
能在同一秒钟把 GPT、Claude 和 Grok 全部按死在地上的，从来不是什么科幻级的黑客大战或 AI 觉醒失控，而是整个人类算力帝国最平庸、最脆弱的底层物理单点寄生。

大众以为这几家巨头拥有各自独立、能够跨地域容灾的神级分布式集群，实际上它们光鲜亮丽的推理入口与能源命脉，全都被焊死在同一批高度中心化的脆弱咽喉上。
 
边缘接入网关与全局路由的共用断头台：不管机房里的模型有多智能，全球用户的 API 调用必须经过极少数几家边缘网络代理与骨干路由。一次全球性的 BGP 路由配置雪崩、根证书级联失效或主流边缘网关崩溃，就能在物理层瞬间阻断所有对外握手；机房里的芯片哪怕毫发无损，也只能在断网的黑暗孤岛里空转。
 
物理机房群与变电走廊的极端地理扎堆：各大巨头表面上分属不同阵营，但为了极限压缩网络延迟与专线成本，全球核心算力与高带宽光缆汇聚点被高度物理压缩在极狭窄的地理走廊内（如北弗吉尼亚数据中心集群）。

区域主干电网的级联跳闸、关键高压变电走廊损毁或主干光纤枢纽的物理断裂，足以在瞬间把所有宣称“高可用”的算力大厂同时断电。
 
 同构软件供应链与驱动层的底层穿刺：顶层大模型看似百家争鸣，底层却高度同构，共用同一套英伟达底层驱动固件、同源的底层推理通信库以及寡头垄断的云端统一鉴权中枢。一次底层内核级的更新事故或共性依赖死锁，就能无视所有上层应用防护，像多米诺骨牌一样击穿所有多云冗余假象。

各大科技巨头心照不宣地在公关通稿里吹嘘分布式架构与绝对弹性，暗地里为了省下跨地域通信的天价带宽账单并换取微秒级的延迟优势，极其默契地把核心资产全部塞进同一个物理漏斗里，对整个行业在基础设施层面的集体裸奔保持绝对死寂。

号称要重塑人类文明的硅基超级大脑，其真实生命线从来没有比几行写错的路由配置或一根烧断的高压电缆更粗壮。

 同构软件供应链与驱动层的底层穿刺：顶层大模型看似百家争鸣，底层却高度同构，共用同一套英伟达底层驱动固件、同源的底层推理通信库以及寡头垄断的云端统一鉴权中枢。一次底层内核级的更新事故或共性依赖死锁，就能无视所有上层应用防护，像多米诺骨牌一样击穿所有多云冗余假象。

各大科技巨头心照不宣地在公关通稿里吹嘘分布式架构与绝对弹性，暗地里为了省下跨地域通信的天价带宽账单并换取微秒级的延迟优势，极其默契地把核心资产全部塞进同一个物理漏斗里，对整个行业在基础设施层面的集体裸奔保持绝对死寂。

号称要重塑人类文明的硅基超级大脑，其真实生命线从来没有比几行写错的路由配置或一根烧断的高压电缆更粗壮。

text:
新旗舰 GPT-6 Astra 刚发布，奥特曼的第一件事不是庆祝，而是发文劝大家“再等等”。

他说得很客气：“我知道大家很着急，感谢大家的耐心，应该很快。”
翻译成大白话其实只有一句：算力被彻底挤爆了。

堂堂顶尖 AI 巨头，新模型上线第一天在干什么？
答案是做极其严苛的限流与分批放行。
首日能摸到模型的，只有极少数被挑中的机构。
至于普通的付费订阅用户，还得在队伍里再排上好几天。

这场防挤兑严密到了什么地步？
就连企业版客户，后台的功能开关默认都是关闭的，得管理员手动去开。
订阅里给的额度根本不够敞开用，超额必须额外花钱买积分。
至于更高级的专业版 Astra Pro，更是只对高阶付费方案开放。

OpenAI 的工程师在后台顶着极限在跑。
为了把模型推给所有 Plus 用户，全新的底层系统第一次承受超大规模并发。
团队正在把所有能调动的物理算力疯狂往上堆。
技术再神仙，撞上物理算力的天花板，巨头也只能按人头限量发号。

text:
拉长时间看，我坚持认为沃什站在了类似于1978年米勒的位置上。

当时，面对大滞胀环境，新总统卡特钦点米勒为美联储主席。米勒坚持配合卡特宽松政策，迟迟不愿提前加息，最终导致了1978、1979年及1980年的大通胀。

我认为，面对当前美国更严峻的债务问题、更大的外部压力以及国内供需不平衡，沃什仍将和1978年的米勒一样，继续配合特朗普的财政政策和地缘政治主张，采取偏宽松或落后于曲线的紧缩政策。

因此，我认为我们正走在通往1978、1979年及1980年二次通胀的道路上。

legacy.full_text:
这几天看孙割真的都有点看腻了，其实还是很多建政圈的老师看的明白，给孙割的定性也很精准。

高中时让女同桌“狠狠拒绝我一次”，她答应了，没想到这句话让他后悔了一辈子

一名网友回忆，高二那年，自己没事犯傻，突然对女同桌说：

“我一会儿向你表白，你狠狠拒绝我一下，让我体验体验什么叫绝望。”

女同桌一脸疑惑地看着他，居然还点了点头。

过了一会儿，他真开始了：

“我喜欢你很久了，想让你做我女朋友，你愿意吗？”

女生瞪大眼睛。

然后当着全班同学的面，认真说了一句：

“我愿意。”

男生当场懵了。

因为按照他们刚才约好的剧本，她明明应该狠狠拒绝自己。

可偏偏，她没有。

很多年以后，他再想起这件事，才慢慢回过味来。

也许当时那个女生根本不是没听懂。

她只是借着这个玩笑，终于把一句真正想说的话说了出来。

可惜那时候的他太迟钝。

现在，他只剩下一句：

“我这辈子最后悔的，就是当时没接住她那句‘我愿意’。”

我姐夫在镇上修了六年电动车，一个月挣6000出头。全家没人看得起他，过年吃饭都没人跟他碰杯。他也不吭声，就坐角落扒拉菜。

我姐也嫌他，说他没本事，挣的还没我多。他也不接话，低头擦那个扳手:手上全是黑的，指甲缝里洗不掉那种。
 
去年我爸住院，查出来要手术，医生说大概15万。我跟弟凑5万，还差10万。我跟姐急得打电话到处借，3天都没借到。

姐夫那天来了穿的还是那件灰夹克，拉链坏了半截。他从兜里掏出一张卡放床头柜上，是他的私房钱，说这里有15万，先用。

我姐愣了我爸躺着也愣了。

15万，修电动车的存了15万。姐夫说每个月花销不了多少，私自存六年，也就攒下来了。

说完他又坐回那个角落去了，跟过年一样。 

我弟后来说他瞧不起姐夫六年了，那天连嘴都张不开。没本事的人真没本事吗？那不叫没本事，那叫不显摆。

text:
🚨OpenCode 联合创始人 Dax Raad 刚刚披露，他们遭遇了一场相当离谱的 Deepfake 诈骗。

他们遭遇了一次相当离谱的诈骗：

有人注册OpenCode的推理服务，直接和销售开视频，自称是一家真实公司的CEO，表示未来一年准备消费40万美元，同时要求团队提高API速率限制。

销售觉得有点不对，还特意去网上搜了这位CEO以前的视频。

结果无论长相还是声音，视频里的人都和真正的CEO几乎一致，一度让他们相信客户是真的。

直到团队继续调查，才发现对方使用的是一个模仿真实公司的域名，而且4天前才注册；调用流量也明显异常，来自海外IP。

团队要求补充身份信息后，对方立刻表示自己马上要上飞机，暂时没法提供，让他们先把额度开了。

最后Dax直接在Instagram联系真正的CEO。

对方完全不知道这件事。

整个视频会议里的CEO，都是骗子实时Deepfake出来的。

这种诈骗其实正在快速升级。2024年，Arup香港办公室一名财务人员参加了一场有CFO和多名同事的视频会议，最终转出约2560万美元，事后才发现会议里除自己之外的人全部是Deepfake。

但现在骗子盯上的已经不只是银行账户，还有AI公司的GPU和Token。

Stripe CEO Patrick Collison今年透露，专门盗用AI算力的Token骗子已经占到一些AI公司每6个新注册用户中的1个。这些人可以用Agent在极短时间内烧掉大量推理额度，然后直接消失。

以前公司遇到可疑客户，最后一道验证方式还是：

开个视频，我看看你是不是本人。

现在连这一层也没了。

脸是真的，声音是真的，公司是真的，CEO也真的存在。

只有正在和你谈生意的那个人是假的。

someone signed up for our inference and did a video call with our sales person confirming intent to spend $400,000 over the next year and asked for increased rate limits

so he figured it was real but we started looking deeper

the email they had been talking to us from was a lookalike domain that was registered 4 days ago. all the traffic they were sending looked bizarre and came from foreign IPs

emailed them for more info to see what they'd say. of course they hit us with the "i'm about to get on a plane, can't do anything right now, please move forward"

messaged the real CEO on instagram and yeah he had no idea what we were talking about, the scammer was deepfaking him

be careful out there, things are getting crazy

销售觉得有点不对，还特意去网上搜了这位CEO以前的视频。

结果无论长相还是声音，视频里的人都和真正的CEO几乎一致，一度让他们相信客户是真的。

直到团队继续调查，才发现对方使用的是一个模仿真实公司的域名，而且4天前才注册；调用流量也明显异常，来自海外IP。

团队要求补充身份信息后，对方立刻表示自己马上要上飞机，暂时没法提供，让他们先把额度开了。

最后Dax直接在Instagram联系真正的CEO。

对方完全不知道这件事。

整个视频会议里的CEO，都是骗子实时Deepfake出来的。

这种诈骗其实正在快速升级。2024年，Arup香港办公室一名财务人员参加了一场有CFO和多名同事的视频会议，最终转出约2560万美元，事后才发现会议里除自己之外的人全部是Deepfake。

但现在骗子盯上的已经不只是银行账户，还有AI公司的GPU和Token。

Stripe CEO Patrick Collison今年透露，专门盗用AI算力的Token骗子已经占到一些AI公司每6个新注册用户中的1个。这些人可以用Agent在极短时间内烧掉大量推理额度，然后直接消失。

以前公司遇到可疑客户，最后一道验证方式还是：

开个视频，我看看你是不是本人。

现在连这一层也没了。

脸是真的，声音是真的，公司是真的，CEO也真的存在。

只有正在和你谈生意的那个人是假的。

text:
IBKR开始取消日内交易了，但很多人可能高兴早了

过去，小于2.5万美元的美股保证金账户，最烦的一条规则就是：5个交易日内，日内交易不能超过3次。

现在FINRA的新规开始落地，IBKR部分账户已经从PDT迁移到新的 Intraday Margin Standards（日内保证金标准）。

最大的变化很直接：

不再数你一天交易多少次，而是看你盘中承担了多大的保证金风险。

也就是说，以后哪怕账户只有1万美元，一天来回交易很多次，本身并不会因为“次数太多”触发PDT。

但这不代表限制消失了。

新的关键词叫：IMD，Intraday Margin Deficit，日内保证金缺口。

简单理解就是以前监管更关心你交易了几次；现在更关心你某个时刻是不是仓位开得太大，保证金缓冲不够了。

在IBKR里，最值得盯的一个指标就是：Current Excess Liquidity

可以把它理解成账户当前距离强平线还有多少缓冲。

IBKR对Excess Liquidity的定义，本质上就是账户权益扣除维持保证金后的剩余空间。

比如：账户权益1万美元。

如果你买入3万美元股票，假设维持保证金率25%，需要7500美元保证金。

那么你理论上还剩：
$10,000 - $7,500 = $2,500

缓冲还在。但如果仓位进一步扩大、股票突然下跌，或者券商临时提高某只股票的保证金率，盘中的保证金缓冲可能快速消失。

这才是新规则真正要管的东西。

美股投资网获悉，高波动股票、杠杆ETF、集中持仓、期权组合，实际保证金要求都可能明显更高。

真正应该留意的是：

Current Excess Liquidity：现在还有多少缓冲

Look Ahead Excess Liquidity：接下来保证金变化后还剩多少

Margin Impact：下一笔订单会吃掉多少保证金

如果真的产生IMD，IBKR要求尽快补足，官方目前给出的指引是最好在3个工作日内解决。

而且如果12个月内多次没有及时补足，达到规定条件后，账户可能被限制90天。

这一单下去，你还剩多少Excess Liquidity？

这才是PDT取消之后，IBKR日内交易最重要的变化。

text:
Broadcom 刚交出了一份惊人的成绩单：单季 AI 芯片收入飙升到 167 亿美元。

但真正震动硅谷的，是财报里披露的一连串客户名字与交付进度。
OpenAI 的第一代自研芯片 Jalapeño 已经在三季度开始出货。
Google 的新一代 TPU v8i 开始量产交付。
Anthropic 锁定了吉瓦级别的专用算力。
它即将在 2027 年成为 Broadcom 最大的自研芯片客户。
这几家在全球大模型竞赛里打得最凶的对手，正在做同一件事：
集体把推理任务，从通用的 GPU 搬到定制的专用芯片上。
为什么连最缺算力的头部实验室，都不再只买 NVIDIA 的显卡？
是旗舰显卡算得不够快，还是底层的经济账已经彻底变了？
把这笔账算到底，会看到一台支配着整个算力世界的冰冷机器。
通用计算税。
通用的图形处理器是按全能标准设计的。
为了应付图形渲染和各种复杂的算法分支，
芯片里塞满了调度单元与冗余电路。
在模型训练阶段，算法天天改，代码随时变。
这种万能的灵活性是必需品。
可一旦模型训练完成，进入全天候的推理服务，情况就彻底变了。
大模型推理做的事情高度固定：
海量的矩阵乘法，加上高带宽的数据搬运。
在通用 GPU 上跑推理，就像雇了一整支交响乐团，天天在路口吹哨指挥交通。
那些用不上的庞大电路依然占着昂贵的晶圆面积，每一毫秒都在空耗电费。
这就是通用计算税：
你为用不上的万能灵活性，付出了几倍的硬件溢价与电力成本。
当算力规模还在几千张卡的时候，没人计较这点损耗。
但当部署规模冲到吉瓦级别，电力成了整个数据中心最硬的物理天花板。
OpenAI 规划在 2027 年部署 1.3 吉瓦的 Jalapeño。
到 2028 年，这个数字要扩张到 5 吉瓦以上。
Anthropic 给出的规划更激进：2028 年要部署 10 吉瓦的专用算力。
在吉瓦级的电网约束面前，算力的较量不再是谁能堆出多高的理论峰值。
核心指标只剩下一个：每一瓦电力，到底能产出多少个标记。
把所有无关的电路全部剥离，只留下最贴合模型结构的计算核与高带宽互联。
这就是 Broadcom 这类芯片设计伙伴搭建的专用机器。
它不负责通用世界里的所有可能性。
它只负责用最低的功耗和成本，把模型推向几亿用户的终端。
AI 行业过去信奉一套军备竞赛叙事，以为护城河全在通用的软硬件生态里。
可当技术从实验室走向工业化量产，
通用的全能，往往会变成最沉重的商业负担。
万能的工具适合探索边界。
但当工业化降临，胜负只取决于谁能把每一度电的浪费剥离到极限。

中年出轨最贵的代价，不只是离婚，而是亲手推翻自己经营了二十年的生活。

小丽有个46岁的闺蜜，结婚整整二十年。

去年，她和麻将桌上认识的男人聊了三个月。聊天记录被丈夫发现后，丈夫在阳台坐了一夜，第二天只说了一句：

“走吧，去办离婚。”

她跪下来解释，说两个人只是聊聊天。

丈夫反问：“三个月、那么多条消息，你管这叫聊聊？”

最后还是离了。

房子是男方婚前买的，15岁的女儿选择跟爸爸生活。她月薪4000元，搬出去租了一间小房子。

以前在家不用操心做饭，丈夫下班后会准备好。现在一个人生活，有时泡面放到坨了，她都没有胃口。

最让她崩溃的是，女儿不接电话，只在微信里说：
“妈妈，你先别找我了。”

她把这句话拿给小丽看时，手一直在抖。

另一个43岁的女人也为了婚外关系结束婚姻，后来和那个男人生活不到三个月，就遭遇了两次家暴。

出轨需要为自己的选择负责，但被打绝不是应得的报应。发现暴力后，首先应该做的是保护自己，尽快离开。

所谓中年人的激情，最容易让人误判的，是只看见新鲜感，却没有计算失去原有生活的成本。

二十年的信任，可能毁在三个月的暧昧里；而那个让你以为遇见爱情的人，未必愿意接住离婚以后全部的现实。

她后来喝醉了，哭着说：
“我不是找到了爱情，是把原来的好日子弄丢了，还伤了孩子。”

婚姻出了问题，可以沟通，也可以体面离开。唯独不要一边享受家庭的稳定，一边拿婚外关系测试自己的运气。

text:
Stop looking at benchmarks for 18 seconds. Watch this.

GPT-6 Astra vs Fable 5.1.

And the difference I find interesting isn’t image quality.

Watch the motion, framing, scene transitions and visual intent on the Astra side.

It doesn’t just feel like a model generating pretty frames.

It feels like something is directing the sequence.

Fable 5.1 looks good.
Astra feels aggressive.

If this level of temporal consistency scales to longer generations, the real GPT-6 story may not be “better video generation.”

It could be something much bigger:

Prompt → cinematography → motion → continuity → finished scene.

We’re getting dangerously close to the point where “generate a video” becomes:

“Direct this scene for me.”

Watch it twice.

Which side would you ship? 👀🔥

text:
大师： 知识库怎么检索？

我： Embedding（向量化）以后做 Vector Search（向量搜索）。

大师： 用户搜 ERR_CONNECTION_RESET_1042 呢？

我： ……向量搜索。

大师： 你确定？

我： 这种错误码、型号、订单号、人名、缩写，BM25 往往更合适。

大师： 为什么？

我： Vector Search（向量搜索）擅长找“意思相近”的内容；BM25 更擅长找“字面上真的出现过”的内容。

大师： 那只用 BM25 不就行了？

我： 也不行。用户问“为什么服务老是断开”，文档里写的是 TCP connection reset，字面不一样，但语义接近，这时候 Vector Search 更有优势。

大师： 所以？

我： 做 Hybrid Search（混合检索）：BM25 找精确词，Vector Search 找语义，再把两边结果融合。

大师： 融合完呢？

我： 再交给 Reranker（重排序模型），把真正相关的文档排到前面。

大师： 那有 Reranker 了，前面随便召回一些不就行？

我： 也不行。Reranker 只能给已经召回的候选重新排序。

大师： 正确答案没召回来呢？

我： 那它也排不出来。

大师： 对。

我： 所以第一阶段 Recall（召回）还是很重要。

大师： 非常重要。

我： 有多重要？

大师： 一堆错答案，也能排得很专业。

青年大学习第55章——做爱姿势完全图鉴：从入门到高阶的20种姿势解析

大部分情侣做爱，来来去去就那几个姿势。
传教士、后入、女上位，循环往复，做到无聊。
不是说这些姿势不好，而是你们根本没有把它们做到位。

姿势描述
她躺在床上，双腿分开，你跪在她两腿之间，进入她。你的身体压在她身上，脸对着脸。

操作要点

男生的位置要比传统传教士更往上一点，让你的耻骨能持续压在她的阴蒂上。
不要大幅度抽插，而是小幅度地前后摇动、碾磨。
重点是"摩擦"而不是"抽插"，保持耻骨和阴蒂的持续接触。

对你：这个姿势能让你更持久，因为不是大力抽插，减少了刺激强度。

常见错误

位置没找对，耻骨没有压在阴蒂上。要多调整几次身体位置。
想要大力抽插。这个技巧的核心是"磨"不是"插"。

3. 蜘蛛体位
姿势描述
女生平躺在床上，双腿微开；男生在女生的上方，女生将双脚夹住男生臀部，形成蜘蛛抱住猎物的姿势。
操作要点

她用双脚夹住你的臀部，可以控制你的抽插节奏和深度。
你的手可以撑在她身体两侧，或者抱着她的腰。
这个姿势能让你们的身体贴得更紧，增加亲密感。

爽点分析

对她：她可以通过双脚控制你的节奏，找到最舒服的角度。
对你：她的双脚夹着你，会让你感觉被"需要"，心理刺激很强。

在她耳边说："夹紧我……别让我出去……"

对你：这个姿势不费力，适合睡前做爱，做完可以直接抱着她睡觉。

这个姿势适合深情对视、接吻、拥抱。

6. 标准后入
姿势描述
她趴在床上或跪着，你跪在她后面，从后面进入她。

让她把腰塌下去、屁股翘起来，这样你能插得更深。

对你：这个姿势能让你看到她的屁股、腰线，视觉刺激很强。

只顾着自己爽，忘记她的感受。后入很容易插得太深、太猛，要随时问她"还可以吗"。
忘记刺激阴蒂。后入时，你的手可以伸到前面，刺激她的阴蒂。

20种做爱姿势，从入门到高阶，每一个都是真实可行的技巧。

那才是真正的做爱。

一名女生发现男朋友主页上有个女生，忍不住问：

“你主页那个姐妹是谁？”

男生回：

“我兄弟。”

女生明显不满意：

“我不喜欢，删了。”

男生却直接拒绝：

“18年为我扛下七八刀，一声没吭。”

女生听完都愣了：

“这么男人？”

男生点点头：

“第一刀砍声带上。”

女生更迷糊了：

“那为什么是姐妹？”

男生淡定回了一句：

“第二刀砍裤裆上了。”

这下全明白了。

不是他故意喊“姐妹”。

是兄弟一路替他扛刀，硬生生把称呼扛变了。

以MU，SNOW甚至当年的HOOD为例，我来阐述一下美股现在基本逻辑：

第一阶段：等你从基本面分析出发好看买入，至少会出现1-2年的深度回调。这段时间热度就没有了，看见其他股票疯狂大涨（美股这么多，总能找到这样的股票），你也觉得自己是个傻逼，决定止损离场

在这个阶段中，只有不跟着kol，不带人炒股，没有任何社交压力的“死人”和“死账号”才能拿住，这种人不超过1%

第二阶段：机构翻牌子，发现大家都跑的差不多了，开始建仓、加仓，股价企稳，但盘面依然半死不活；然后，在一个财报利好发布后，股价突然暴涨20%，40%，甚至100%。

第三阶段：因为股价大涨，热度回升，kol和投资社群开始重新关注这只股票，各类散户才开始纷纷上车，最终高位接盘，变成机构的韭菜

text:
我说的，可能是个违反大部分人直觉的想法：我认为将来私有化部署的开源模型 Kimi、GLM、DeepSeek 的需求，可能远大于 Fable、GPT 这类顶尖模型

我举个例子，大家就能懂这些顶级模型在日常工作中与我的关系：

1. Fable5.1：顶级聪明，名校毕业，智力超群，但问题是工资太高，高到我支付不起，而且有脾气，遇到不符合它心中标准的就不好好干，默默降智

2. GPT 5.6：能力卓越，勤劳肯干，能够很好地胜任大部分工作，但心中仍有道德感，会拒绝一些违反公序良俗的请求

3. 私有部署的开源kimi/deepseek模型：我相信这才是大部分人最想要的。它可以成为私人的嫡系，尽管他不是最聪明的，但是所有的脏活、累活、见不得人的都可以聊，可以做，数据天知地知你知我知。

虽然私有部署没有前面那些那么聪明，但是可以和你彻底成为同一战线，真正成为自己人

那么问题来了：如果你有一个工作，你愿意交给自己人来做，还是交给那些顶级聪明、但可能没有完全同一战线的人来做呢？

quotedTweet.text:
Fable5.1如期发布，高强度用了一个下午，分享一下我的一手体验：

大部分人不需要一个“神一样聪明”的模型，普通人的AGI在opus4.8/gpt5.6 的时候已经到了。现在缺的是，足够便宜

今天下午我让 Fable 5.1 给我的项目写文档，一个query直接烧掉我 $200/月会员一周额度的 38%。

但我主观感觉，写出来的东西确实比 GPT-5.6 Sol 好大概 1.2 倍

从opus4.8时代开始AI已经可以读 repo、debug、写代码、写文档，操作Excel，那对绝大多数人来说，intelligence 可能已经够用了

想象一下，当这种级别的模型可以私有化部署，一天随便烧几千万 token，你根本不用考虑额度，让它 24 小时读代码、跑实验、写文档、做研究……

那可能才是真正的生产力爆发。

所以我现在越来越看好的不是单纯继续 scale intelligence，

而是 Inference Cost ↓ + 私有化部署 ↑

text:
这篇写得真好呀。

它讲了一个特别有意思的类比：

今天我们对 Agent 的想象，很可能就像 1995 年的人对互联网的想象一样。方向完全对，但把最终的产品形态猜错了。

当年所有人都知道互联网会爆发，也知道每个人都会在网上表达自己。

但他们以为，未来每个人都会拥有一个自己的网站。

结果并没有。

真正覆盖几十亿人的，是 Facebook、Instagram、TikTok。

大家确实都有了自己的“个人主页”，只是绝大多数人根本不需要碰 HTML 和 JavaScript。

作者认为 Agent 也会发生同样的事情。

未来每个人都会使用 Agent。

但真正直接使用 Coding Agent 的，可能永远不到 1%。

今天我们觉得 Agent 应该拥有浏览器、Shell、文件系统和各种权限，可以自由地在电脑上完成任何事情。

这就像当年觉得每个人都应该拥有一个网站一样。

对于极少数技术人员来说，这种自由度非常爽。

但对于几十亿普通用户来说，问题根本不是“Agent 够不够聪明”，而是：

我敢不敢放心把事情交给它。

它不能误付款，不能误发消息，不能读取不该读取的数据。

而且这些事情不能只是“概率很低”。

必须从系统上做到根本不可能发生。

所以真正决定 Agent 能不能进入几十亿人生活的，可能不是模型能力继续涨多少。

而是能不能找到 Agent 世界里的那个“社交媒体”。

把一个开放、复杂、危险的通用计算环境，压缩成几个极其简单、可预测、安全的操作。

就像互联网从“人人建网站”，最后 collapse 成了发文字、图片和视频。

Agent 也可能发生一次这样的 collapse。

未来你当然每天都在用 Agent。

但你可能从来不会打开一个 Coding Agent。

你只是跟微信说一句“帮我约今晚吃饭”，跟淘宝说“把这几个异常订单处理一下”。

我敢不敢放心把事情交给它。

text:
朋友被裁员后，在家躺了几个月。

最近看别人摆摊卖卤味赚钱，他突然来了劲，准备花3万多拜师，把配方和三轮车一起买下来。

妻子坚决反对，怕他工作没找到，存款又先亏光。

有人给他出了个主意：

先别交学费，也别买设备。

去师傅的摊位买几百块钱卤味，租辆三轮车，换个地方按10元一份卖，连续试5天。

卖得动，说明当地确实有需求，再考虑花钱学技术；卖不动，剩下的卤味拿回家下酒，几百块就买到了答案。

创业最重要的第一步，不是辞职、拜师和买设备，而是用最小的成本证明真的有人愿意掏钱。

很多人失败，不是产品做得不好，而是市场还没验证，就把学费、房租、装修和设备一次性全投了进去。

真正聪明的创业，不是上来就押重注，而是先用500元试错，再决定要不要投入3万元。

如果是你，会直接拜师开摊，还是先卖5天试试？

text:
47岁的新加坡国立大学教授何迪安 Dean Ho，生物年龄测出来只有31.8岁。

从2021年到2024年，3年的时间里, 两次体检，到底发生了什么？

教授在大约8个月里同时佩戴了Whoop、Garmin和Apple Watch三种可穿戴设备，并结合血糖、血酮、血脂、炎症指标、血压、心率、HRV、运动表现、睡眠和肠道菌群等信息进行长期追踪。

这是他的总结：

→ 吃饭集中在4小时左右

Dean Ho教授每天大约有20小时处于禁食状态，主要把进食集中在上午11点到下午3点左右，期间还进行了多次48小时的禁食，用来观察不同禁食状态下身体的反应。

→ 蔬菜、蛋白质、健康脂肪为主

→ 每周至少练2次肌肉

→ 把睡觉时间提前近3小时

Dean Ho教授过去大约午夜以后睡觉。

DELTA启动后，睡眠方案把上床时间提前到了晚上约9点15分，同时安排早晨运动、取消下午小睡、减少睡前屏幕，并把最后一杯咖啡提前到早上7—8点。

总睡眠从过去大约6.2小时增加到接近8.2小时，同时REM睡眠和深睡时间有所增加，夜间清醒时间下降。

→肠道菌群也被纳入监测

附图：新加坡国立大学何迪安Dean Ho教授2021 年（左）和 2024 年（右）的照片

文章来自：瘦龙健康

result.text:
47岁的新加坡国立大学教授何迪安 Dean Ho，生物年龄测出来只有31.8岁。

从2021年到2024年，3年的时间里, 两次体检，到底发生了什么？

教授在大约8个月里同时佩戴了Whoop、Garmin和Apple Watch三种可穿戴设备，并结合血糖、血酮、血脂、炎症指标、血压、心率、HRV、运动表现、睡眠和肠道菌群等信息进行长期追踪。

这是他的总结：

→ 吃饭集中在4小时左右

Dean Ho教授每天大约有20小时处于禁食状态，主要把进食集中在上午11点到下午3点左右，期间还进行了多次48小时的禁食，用来观察不同禁食状态下身体的反应。

→ 蔬菜、蛋白质、健康脂肪为主

→ 每周至少练2次肌肉

→ 把睡觉时间提前近3小时

Dean Ho教授过去大约午夜以后睡觉。

DELTA启动后，睡眠方案把上床时间提前到了晚上约9点15分，同时安排早晨运动、取消下午小睡、减少睡前屏幕，并把最后一杯咖啡提前到早上7—8点。

总睡眠从过去大约6.2小时增加到接近8.2小时，同时REM睡眠和深睡时间有所增加，夜间清醒时间下降。

→肠道菌群也被纳入监测

附图：新加坡国立大学何迪安Dean Ho教授2021 年（左）和 2024 年（右）的照片

文章来自：瘦龙健康

GPT-6 Astra represents a step-function change in model capability for interactive reasoning problems. It scores 66% on ARC-AGI-3 using our standard harness, and nearly 100% with a continuous conversation harness and custom compaction, at a cost of roughly $360 per game.

In fact, the continuous harness version significantly outperforms our human baseline in action efficiency across almost all levels. When we examined the reasoning chains to understand how the model operates, we found it performing highly efficient, on-the-fly symbolic world modeling for each game and level. It goes as far as developing its own shorthand DSL to represent in-game situations -- essentially a game-specific algebraic notation.

Overall, Astra exhibits symbolic modeling behaviors we had previously only seen with sophisticated harnesses -- so harness capabilities are increasingly shifting into the model itself.

We see Astra as a major breakthrough in model intelligence.

Read our post on Astra and what these results mean: https://t.co/wJnYxEqYNI

text:
⚡️The line has moved from execution into judgment.

That is the real event.

Astra is showing signs of doing something much more dangerous to professional labor than writing faster, coding better, or summarizing more documents.

It is beginning to police the validity of its own conclusions.

It sees a proxy and refuses to call it the real metric.

It sees strange data and refuses to call it missing.

It reaches a legal conclusion and asks what provision actually authorizes that conclusion.

It detects that the answer can be superficially correct while the structure underneath it is wrong.

That is senior-level cognition.

For decades, the professional hierarchy worked because junior people produced analysis and experienced people caught the subtle category errors hiding inside it.

AI is beginning to perform both sides of that loop.

Produce the work. Then audit the work.

Once that becomes reliable, the economic architecture changes brutally.

The junior pyramid contracts because machines handle execution.

The middle contracts because machines coordinate and synthesize.

The senior layer loses part of its scarcity because machines increasingly catch the errors that justified senior review.

What remains human for longer is authority, responsibility, taste, consequence, political judgment, and the genuinely novel edge cases where reality has not supplied enough precedent.

That is a much smaller surface area.

And there is one feature here that matters more than every benchmark number:

Astra appears better at refusing false certainty.

That is enormous.

Intelligence becomes dangerous and economically valuable when it can say:

“I have enough evidence.”

“I do not have enough evidence.”

“This conclusion follows.”

“This one only looks like it follows.”

That boundary is where judgment lives.

If models keep improving there, the white-collar disruption accelerates much faster than people expecting a chatbot revolution understand.

Because corporations do not need AI to become omniscient.

They need AI to become reliable enough that one human can supervise what ten humans used to produce.

Astra looks like another step toward exactly that threshold.

And the deepest signal is this:

The machine is learning when the map no longer deserves to be trusted.

Once intelligence can question the representation placed in front of it, it has crossed into the territory humans used to call expertise.

The next frontier is no longer whether AI can produce the answer.

It is whether AI can recognize when the answer should not be believed.

That is where professional scarcity starts dying.

quotedTweet.text:
GPT-6 Astra is out. We've been testing the model in early preview on our enterprise complex work eval at Box. It is now the best model we've ever tested on our expanded and hardest test set.

Overall, GPT-6 Astra offers a breakthrough level of capability in coding, analytics, logic, and domain specific knowledge for dealing with complex enterprise knowledge work. In our eval, we use the GPT-6 Astra model in the Box Agent and give it a set of difficult tasks that represent real-world work in various industries. These tasks often will take people hours to execute properly and require deep domain expertise.

GPT-6 Astra scored 77% overall vs. 74% with GPT-5.6 Sol, representing frontier performance. But the story is in some of the bigger gains on individual task types that are incredibly complex across. Here are a few examples across the tests that show how much of an impact this will be in different industries:

* Media and entertainment (48% → 100%, +52 points). Ranking film genres and countries by profitability across a year of production data from four teams, where the trick is to apply the following year's tax-incentive corrections without double-counting them. GPT-6 Astra was perfect on every attempt. Sol had the rankings right but the underlying ratios were wrong.

* Technology (69% → 97%, +28 points). Choosing which region to fund first, from a stack of performance and infrastructure documents that never state the metric the brief asks for. GPT-6 Astra flagged the gap, labelled its own figure a proxy, and caught a growth claim that didn't match the numbers beneath it. GPT-5.6 Sol reported the proxy as the real thing.

* Legal (69% → 93%, +24 points). Reviewing an NDA against a company's own contracting policy, where reaching the right verdict isn't enough; the answer has to cite the provision behind it. Both models declined to approve the draft, but only GPT-6 Astra separated whether the liability cap's structure was permissible from whether its amount was defensible, and pointed to the policy language that settles it. GPT-5.6 Sol argued the same conclusion without citing the provision, which is a critical error in the legal industry.

* Healthcare (53% → 77%, +23 points). Auditing a batch of radiology reports for errors and rating how serious each one is. GPT-6 Astra caught a terminology error in a knee-imaging report that GPT-5.6 Sol missed on both attempts, and was more reliable at grading severity rather than just flagging that something was wrong.

* Energy (82% → 97%, +15 points). Building a consumption report on two facilities from a year of meter logs, where only one of the two sites is actually missing data. GPT-6 Astra found it and drew a line most reviewers wouldn't: the other site's odd solar readings are a measurement problem to investigate, not a gap in the record. GPT-5.6 Sol reported both sites as incomplete.

Astra clearly is going to offer a meaningful jump in powering and orchestrating enterprise workflows. We'll be making GPT-6 Astra as an option in the Box AI Studio for customers to build agents with shortly as it continues to roll out.

现在看来，袁腾飞老师润美消息大概率为真。不到一天之前，袁老师的频道《LIFEANO CLUB》发表了一期节目《袁sir聊北京行动：只有润出来，复国才有希望！》“北京行动”是二战前夕波兰海军的一次撤离行动，为波兰保存了有限的海上实力。
这期节目似乎在呼应袁老师已经“润出来”的传闻。如果消息为真，在这里祝贺袁老师及家人！如果此次是举家迁移，当然涉及家人安顿等一系列事，要花一段时间，也祝愿一切顺利。
在自媒体这个领域，袁腾飞老师、老梁和大眼哥都是我的前辈。在我还在念研究生的时候，大眼哥就名满天下了。我在做自媒体的早期，也从诸位前辈大咖身上获益很多，也是踏着前辈的路走过来的。我的自媒体早期，多次谈到从袁老师、罗振宇、老梁身上所学到的。虽然观点未必都一致，但始终以前辈达人看待诸位，也心怀感激。
诸位前辈润美、润加以后，也会带出来一部分中国观众的注意力，也会对其他同行起到鼓励作用，当然是好事。不过中共也不会对此无视，最常见的是：拿身处海外的意见领袖的国内亲人下手——比如父母，要挟意见领袖妥协。
有时是要求你戴上无形的枷锁，继续自我审查；有时是允许你发表批评，但在某些时刻、某些话题要配合。国内的影响力越大，当局遥制的意图就越强。这种事在海外舆论场我们已经屡见不鲜了。
所以肉身翻墙是第一步，身处海外的名人、意见领袖们还会面临许多艰辛、与煎熬。脚下的路仍然漫长崎曲，不同人会有不同的选择。
再次祝贺袁腾飞老师、老梁（如果传闻也为真的话）出境成功。祝各位在新舞台上能直抒胸臆，事业红火！

现在看来，袁腾飞老师润美消息大概率为真。不到一天之前，袁老师的频道《LIFEANO CLUB》发表了一期节目《袁sir聊北京行动：只有润出来，复国才有希望！》“北京行动”是二战前夕波兰海军的一次撤离行动，为波兰保存了有限的海上实力。
这期节目似乎在呼应袁老师已经“润出来”的传闻。如果消息为真，在这里祝贺袁老师及家人！如果此次是举家迁移，当然涉及家人安顿等一系列事，要花一段时间，也祝愿一切顺利。
在自媒体这个领域，袁腾飞老师、老梁和大眼哥都是我的前辈。在我还在念研究生的时候，大眼哥就名满天下了。我在做自媒体的早期，也从诸位前辈大咖身上获益很多，也是踏着前辈的路走过来的。我的自媒体早期，多次谈到从袁老师、罗振宇、老梁身上所学到的。虽然观点未必都一致，但始终以前辈达人看待诸位，也心怀感激。
诸位前辈润美、润加以后，也会带出来一部分中国观众的注意力，也会对其他同行起到鼓励作用，当然是好事。不过中共也不会对此无视，最常见的是：拿身处海外的意见领袖的国内亲人下手——比如父母，要挟意见领袖妥协。
有时是要求你戴上无形的枷锁，继续自我审查；有时是允许你发表批评，但在某些时刻、某些话题要配合。国内的影响力越大，当局遥制的意图就越强。这种事在海外舆论场我们已经屡见不鲜了。
所以肉身翻墙是第一步，身处海外的名人、意见领袖们还会面临许多艰辛、与煎熬。脚下的路仍然漫长崎曲，不同人会有不同的选择。
再次祝贺袁腾飞老师、老梁（如果传闻也为真的话）出境成功。祝各位在新舞台上能直抒胸臆，事业红火！

新来男同事长得太帅，女同事集体围上去问姓什么，结果他最后一句全办公室炸了

公司新来了个男同事，长得人模狗样，刚坐下没多久，几个女同事就围了上来。

大姐最先开口：

“帅哥，贵姓啊？”

男同事笑了笑，没直接说，反而伸出两根手指搓了搓，做了个数钱的手势。

大姐眼睛一亮：

“姓数？数学的数？”

男同事摇头。

二姐赶紧接：

“那姓搓？搓麻将的搓？”

男同事脸都快绿了：

“你们能不能往值钱的方向想？”

三姐压低声音，小心翼翼地问：

“姓金？黄金的金？”

男同事深吸一口气：

“再猜，最后一次机会。”

整个办公室瞬间安静了三秒。

然后他一拍桌子：

“我姓钱！金钱的钱！”

全办公室当场笑翻。

大姐一拍大腿：

“早说啊，我还以为你姓穷呢，难怪一直不敢说。”

text:
昨天跟我兄弟聊天，聊着聊着他突然冒出一句：「我前阵子去打了龟头玻尿酸。」我当场愣了一下，马上开始追问他到底是什么感觉。

他说一开始最担心的是打完会不会很假，结果实际看起来并不会，比较像是在原本的基础上等比例放大，整体自然很多，不会有那种一眼就看得出来「有动过」的感觉。

我也问他会不会影响勃起，他说完全不会。因为玻尿酸是打在龟头本身，不会影响海绵体，所以勃起功能还是正常。

效果方面，医生说一般可以维持约1～3年，比脸部玻尿酸的维持时间还要长。如果另一半本来就很熟悉你的尺寸，变大后还是有可能察觉，不过整体看起来还是很自然。

我最后还问了一个大家最关心的问题：「那多久才能恢复正常使用？」他说打完只有一些小针孔，等伤口慢慢愈合、形状稳定后，大约3周就可以恢复正常使用，不用休息太久。

说真的，要不是听他亲口分享，我还真不知道玻尿酸可以打龟头上。

我也问他会不会影响勃起，他说完全不会。因为玻尿酸是打在龟头本身，不会影响海绵体，所以勃起功能还是正常。

效果方面，医生说一般可以维持约1～3年，比脸部玻尿酸的维持时间还要长。如果另一半本来就很熟悉你的尺寸，变大后还是有可能察觉，不过整体看起来还是很自然。

我最后还问了一个大家最关心的问题：「那多久才能恢复正常使用？」他说打完只有一些小针孔，等伤口慢慢愈合、形状稳定后，大约3周就可以恢复正常使用，不用休息太久。

说真的，要不是听他亲口分享，我还真不知道玻尿酸可以打龟头上。

text:
葫芦娃其实是最早的 MoE 架构。

七个兄弟是挂在同一个系统里的七个 specialized experts：大娃负责力量和体型扩展，二娃负责视觉与听觉感知，三娃负责高防御，四娃、五娃分别处理火系和水系能力，六娃负责隐身，七娃则直接持有高权限法器。

这套系统的问题从来不是 expert 不够强，而是 router 太差。

每次遇到任务，系统都会根据当前问题激活一个看起来最匹配的 expert，然后让他单独进入副本。结果就是单专家能力很强，但跨专家协同极差：二娃明明已经完成环境感知，却没有把 observation 写入 shared memory；三娃有防御能力，却没有承担 tank；四娃和五娃本可以做组合控制，偏偏始终串行调用。

这就是典型的 MoE 利用率问题：expert specialization 做得很好，orchestration 几乎没有。

而且蛇精很快发现了这个漏洞。她根本不需要正面打赢整个系统，只需要针对当前激活的 expert 做 adversarial routing，把每个葫芦娃分别诱导进自己最不擅长的任务空间，就能逐个击破。

所以真正完成系统升级的，不是某一个葫芦娃继续 scaling，而是最后七个 expert 融合成葫芦小金刚，第一次把 perception、planning、defense、tool use 和 execution 压进了同一个统一策略里。

大家小时候以为《葫芦兄弟》讲七兄弟救爷爷。

长大以后才发现，它讲的是一个 MoE 系统，因为 router 和 agent orchestration 没做好，被 prompt injection 打到反复团灭。

说实话，我做空啥都不怕，但我挺怕特朗普那张嘴。

今天有两个消息在推美股。

第一个，是美联储官员释放了相对偏温和的信号，认为目前通胀情况符合预期，接下来CPI会变得非常关键。加息概率下降到50%

第二个就更直接了。

特朗普盘前又出来喊：

不管你信不信，股票会涨。

给我整蒙了 我是真的想相信 看着我一把空单我恍然间迷茫了哈哈哈

因为以前特朗普类似的喊话出来，市场确实经常会给反应。

所以说实话：

我啥都不怕，但我挺怕特朗普那张嘴。😂

回归理性

这些消息有没有改变我这一轮做空的底层逻辑？

没有。

所以今天：

仓位没有变化。

空单继续持有。

甚至我还在继续增加 $UVXY 的仓位。

为什么？

因为我前几天一直在讲的那个问题，到今天依然没有答案：

如果美联储不加息，那你准备怎么让债券市场相信，你能够控制长期通胀？

这一轮市场为什么会跌？

恰恰就是因为市场开始担心：

美联储不愿意进一步收紧。

于是债券市场自己要求更高的收益率。

结果就是：

不加息 → 长债收益率上升 → 无风险利率上升 → 股票估值被压。

那现在如果答案还是：

不加息。

问题不就又回到原点了吗？

如果长债没有解决，市场凭什么重新打开持续创新高的估值空间？

所以我的逻辑一点没变：

不是“加息”这两个字让我看空。

我真正盯的是：

债券市场到底信不信美联储。

⸻

现在10年期美债收益率已经来到 4.8%附近。

4.8%本身就是一个比较明显的压力区域，所以这里出现阶段性回落，我一点都不意外。

但我目前依然倾向于：

4.8%未必是终点。

我还是在看：

10Y突破4.8%，继续向5%靠近。

而这里又很反人性。

很多人会觉得：

收益率5%了，不应该更危险吗？

但在我的交易框架里，真正逼近5%的时候，反而可能是我开始认真寻找反转、重新做多机会的时候。

因为到了那个位置，市场对于美联储和财政端采取更强政策动作的预期会明显提高。

换句话说：

从现在到5%的过程，我担心的是估值继续被压。

真正到5%附近，我反而开始准备找多头机会。

所以目前我的计划依然非常清晰：

空单继续。
UVXY继续布局。
不因为一天的利好消息改变方向。

什么时候改变？

不是特朗普喊一句“股票会涨”。

也不是市场一天反弹。

而是：

长债真正告诉我——市场重新开始相信Fed了。

不过uvxy挺有毒的 拿着风险是比较高的。我买了差不多30万的 还是为了博暴力拉升。

3、卡尼跟川普直接通话了好几次，我就在总统身边，他们达成了共识。总统还发了Truth推文：我们有协议了。我们这些下属就着手收尾、搞定细节。

text:
大家默认 奥特曼的Whisper 是 语音识别（ASR） 天花板。

我用四川话测了一句：巴适。
Whisper 听成了八式，它从没学过四川话。
同一批音频，Hojo-ASR-Multi-V1：错误率0.0%。

接着，我给了它们一段成都街头的环境音，全程没有一个人说话。
· Whisper 吐出 100 个 嗨
· Hojo 吐出 5 个字符

两个都幻觉了，但一个是 100 字，一个是 5 字。嘈杂街头声音解码，是常用的场景。
我用两个模型做了详细评测。最有意思的是 Hojo 的底座 —— 语音编码器来自 Qwen3-Omni-30B，语言解码器是 Qwen3-4B。

🚀一个文本大模型，凭什么能做语音识别？

因为 ASR 从来就是两半：声学 + 语言。
「bā shì」这个音，在波形里根本分不出是「巴适」还是「八式」—— 声音里没有这个信息。能定夺的只有语言知识：哪个词真的存在、在这个语境里说得通。

Qwen3-4B 读过整个中文互联网，知道「巴适」是个四川话词。

🔥接法很巧：训练一个适配器，把音频编码成2560维向量，刚好Qwen3-4B刚好接受2560 维。

两个数字一对上，Qwen 就以为自己在读词，其实在听声音。
所以这不是从头训语音识别模型，而是后训练：拿 Qwen3-4B 当初始化权重，连同音频编码器一起全参数微调。
我把它的解码器和原版 Qwen3-4B 逐层比对过，每一层都有变化。所以不是白嫖 Qwen 的语言知识，避免了从零预训练语言能力。这条路叫 Encoder-Adapter-LLM。

最后还有一个牛逼的点：
Open ASR Leaderboard全球第 7，开源多语言 ASR 第 1。
五语种平均 WER 3.54%，而且权重开放、评测公开、结果可复现。
现已支持四川话、广东话小语种。

Apache 2.0 开源。
https://t.co/47I73Y5Ah5

text:
媒体报道: 习近平为了化解可能导致中国政府系统性崩溃风险的地方债问题, 将新冠肺炎期间的动态清零策略用到了地方政府化债工作中. 近日, 习近平颁布了一条激进的政治命令, 他要求地方各级党委政府必须在2027年6月底前, 将地方融资平台要全面退出; 2028年底前将地方政府隐性债务要全部“清零”, 业内称之为“双清零”. 

 “动态清零”政策的特点之一就是外行领导内行, 因为不懂问题的复杂性, 干脆用一刀切的方式处理问题, 好处就是简单, 坏处就是粗暴. 简单粗暴, 其实就是习近平的治国理念, 至少是下意识里的治国理念, 遇到问题这个理念就会自然而然地成为他的政策选择. 过去处理疫情时这样的, 现在要化解地方债问题, 结果又是这样. 这证明了习近平面对层出不穷的新问题, 还是只能运用旧思维. 

问题是, 简单的思维能够解决问题吗? 答案很明显, 不能. 疫情问题已经是先例: 最终还是放弃了清零政策, 以具有习近平特色的“烂尾”方式看着一清自己结束.我们可以预料, 用“清零”的手法去处理地方债问题, 结果一定还是一样:烂尾.

地方债问题由来已久, 归根结底还是制度本身的问题. 地方官员不靠选举靠任命, 他对上负责不对下负责, 因此势必要靠肉眼可见的基础设施建设来树立所谓的政绩, 至于这些基础设施的使用情况和盈亏状况, 那是下一任的事情, 他只要能因此升官就好. 搞大搞工程来博取仕途, 这是刚需. 你不让地方政府想办法自己搞钱来谋取自己的前途, 他为什么还给你干活? 

习近平自认为一言九鼎, 他按理说应当知道, 中国官场上那些人都是老油条, 几十年来中南海出了无数政策, 下到地方能够落实的能有几条? 地方债清零也将是如此, 地方官员一定能找出办法规避上面的指标. 在这一点上,我对他们有信心.

因此, 这一轮地方债清零, 听起来雷厉风行, 但最后的结果, 一定是不了了之. 你以为“烂尾帝”的称号是白给的吗?

@baodiantimes

text:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.

Here's a full recap:

1. Broadcom $AVGO said it has a “high degree of confidence” it will ship $350B of AI semiconductors over the next 2 years, even if all 30 GW of demand is not deployed because of land, power, and data center constraints. The company laid out a massive AI growth path, targeting AI semiconductor revenue of roughly $58B in FY26, $115B in FY27, and $230B in FY28 — a 4x increase in just 2 years. Broadcom said every 1 GW deployed by OpenAI or Anthropic could support about $30B in annual AI revenue, while AI networking revenue is expected to grow just as fast as its XPU business. In Q3’26, Broadcom reported revenue of $29.6B, beating estimates of $29.36B and up 86% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $3.32 versus $3.24 expected. AI semiconductor revenue surged 221% YoY to $16.7B, and Broadcom expects that to accelerate to $21.7B in Q4, up 236% YoY, while also targeting $30+ EPS in FY28.

2. Meta $META rolled out Muse Spark 1.3, saying the latest model delivers its biggest coding and agentic performance jump yet. Meta says Muse Spark 1.3 matches GPT-5.6 Sol on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with a score of 88.8 and reaches 75.4 on DeepSWE. The model is available now through Muse Code and the API. Zuckerberg also teased Watermelon and open weights coming next, signaling Meta is continuing to push aggressively on frontier coding agents and open AI distribution.

3. Nvidia-backed neocloud Nscale is telling prospective IPO investors it has roughly $103B in contracted revenue, up from $51B before its $45B compute deal with Anthropic, according to The Information. The contracts average 5.7 years, implying about $18B of future contracted revenue per year, though the figure is not current revenue or formal guidance and was described by one source as “illustrative.” Actual revenue is still much smaller but scaling quickly, rising from about $37M in Q1 2026 to more than $100M in Q2, excluding the Anthropic deal, as Nscale prepares for an IPO that could come as soon as this month.

4. HPE $HPE expanded its Oracle $ORCL AI data center deal, with HPE set to deploy Juniper networking gear across Oracle AI data centers globally under a potential multi-year agreement. The deal covers routing, switching, networking support, and financing for OCI’s AI clusters, regional data centers, and edge networks, while HPE also issued Oracle warrants to purchase HPE shares. Separately, HPE reported Q3’26 revenue of $12.2B, beating estimates of $11.91B and up 34% YoY, with adjusted EPS of $1.11 versus $0.93 expected. Networking revenue surged 74.9% YoY to $2.9B, while Cloud & AI revenue rose 25.4% YoY to $9.0B. HPE guided Q4 revenue to $13.9B–$14.8B, above the $12.96B estimate, raised FY26 guidance, and said AI is becoming a multi-year growth driver as record backlog supports the outlook.

5. Cantor Fitzgerald initiated Tempus $TEM at Overweight with an $80 price target, arguing the company is being mispriced as a traditional life sciences data vendor rather than an AI-powered platform business. The firm says Tempus’ Data & Applications segment has a stronger growth and margin profile than the market is giving it credit for, with 26% growth and 76% gross margins. Cantor believes the segment should be compared more closely to platform peers like $PLTR, $SNOW, $DDOG, and $RDDT rather than slower-growing data-vendor peers, creating a favorable upside risk/reward.

6. Google $GOOGL launched Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a new cybersecurity-focused AI model that scored 86.2% on CyberGym and 47.2% on CWE-Bench. Google says the model has a 70%+ success rate identifying vulnerabilities across 20 programming languages and produced 2.6x more correct patches than larger models on real Chrome security bugs. Initial access is limited to government agencies and cybersecurity partners through Google’s Fairwind program.

7. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 5.7M contracts, $TSLA with 2.8M contracts, $AAPL with 1.7M contracts, $META with 1.0M contracts, $MU with 959K contracts, $AMZN with 732K contracts, $PLTR with 675K contracts, $DELL with 633K contracts, $INTC with 557K contracts, and $GOOGL with 536K contracts.

8. JPMorgan says a 5% 10-year Treasury yield could be the level that starts to pressure stocks, with Grace Peters noting that “5% psychologically has an impact” and could trigger a knee-jerk equity selloff. She sees a potential 5%-8% correction into the midterms, but views that as a healthy pullback rather than a structural break. JPMorgan remains constructive on stocks longer term, with its thesis centered on a capex-driven earnings supercycle, while the key medium-term test for AI will be whether the spending translates into real returns.

9. Berenberg initiated Rocket Lab $RKLB at Buy with an $83 price target, implying about 29%-35% upside, calling it the only end-to-end public pure-play in space across launch, satellites, components, and spectrum. The firm says Rocket Lab has an effective monopoly in dedicated small-lift launch, is entering medium-lift with Neutron, and is benefiting from rapid growth in satellite manufacturing and components as space budgets hit records. Berenberg also said the Iridium acquisition adds scarce global spectrum and recurring applications revenue, while Rocket Lab’s vertical integration gives it long-term optionality not fully reflected in the stock’s valuation. While acknowledging execution risk and a high multiple, the firm called Rocket Lab one of the most compelling long-term assets in the space sector and said it would buy or add on volatility.

10. The 60+ day delinquency rate on U.S. subprime auto loans has climbed to roughly 5.2%, the highest level on record and more than double where it was four years ago. Serious subprime auto delinquencies are now about 1.7 percentage points above their 2008 financial crisis peak, while prime auto loan delinquencies have also risen to around 0.4%, near the highest level since 2011. At the same time, total U.S. auto debt increased by $28B in Q2 2026 to a record $1.71T.

11. Onchain tokenized equity holders have reached a record 1.9M, up 134% month-over-month and 1,360% year-to-date. Just 10 months ago, fewer than 100,000 people held tokenized assets, but demand for 24/7 markets and access to names tied to the record IPO wave, including SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic, has accelerated adoption. Jupiter, the largest onchain trading platform on Solana, has driven much of the growth, with 61% of volume now happening during off-hours and active tokenized equity traders up 46% month-over-month.

12. Microsoft $MSFT will begin disclosing Azure revenue as part of a major FY27 reporting overhaul, shifting from three business segments to two: Agents & Infrastructure and Devices & Consumer. For Q1 FY27, Microsoft expects Azure growth of 44%-45% in constant currency, Agents & Infrastructure revenue of $75.15B-$75.75B, Devices & Consumer revenue of $14.7B-$15.2B, Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud growth of about 17% in constant currency, and Search & Ads ex-TAC growth in the mid-to-high single digits. The new structure marks Microsoft’s biggest reporting change since adopting its prior three-segment model in FY2016.

WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

text:
Michael Burry这种AI空头，看企业更不行，他买的什么垃圾？

$LULU 财报全面不及预期，收入降，毛利降，费用还升，一无是处。

这公司从去年，我最早就评论底层逻辑在于消费美学和文化变迁

过去那套瑜伽风、打着“多元”旗号的丑模特广告，现在已经失去号召力。

市场情绪在转，审美也在转，从“丑也要被看见”慢慢回到“性感、叛逆才有吸引力”。

一个靠看穿泡沫成名的人，竟然看不懂一条瑜伽裤已经不性感了。

$LULU 财报盘后大跌18年历史低点，是大空头Burry的爱股

这种投资水平，不懂科技半导体和芯片也就算了，毕竟不是工程专业

但是客流/单价/转化/同店销售核心指标

随便不是脑残的都知道，到店里看看看不懂，什么是“美”？

北美大本营谁还穿？

年轻人觉得过气，年纪大的还觉得不舒适，我现在一身休闲穿的，有些还是十年前的Lululemon都比现在还有型

这种投资者就是一辈子靠08房贷一个事情装x，赢者的诅咒，不好好学习，人没老，脑子先僵化了

text:
Side note: when we released ARC-AGI-3 in March, and frontier models scored <1% on it, a few Singularitarian poasters took it as a personal insult, and got very worked up about it. They argued the benchmark was fundamentally broken, that it could not even be solved by the smartest humans, that the max reachable score was actually 40%, etc.

We had to deal with a torrent of insults and hate poasts since because we had released an unsaturated benchmark.

As it turns out, the benchmark is perfectly calibrated. It is straightforward for a human to score 100% if they do better than average people – all you need is to use fewer actions than our human baseline (which is not a strong baseline, as we used unfiltered human testers).

And naturally as a result it's also very feasible for AI to score 100% once real progress towards agentic general intelligence has been made. The trajectory of AI from <1% to 100% over the course of 6 months shows that the benchmark was able to snapshot the recent rise of agentic capabilities. And that rise has happened faster than most people expected, including us.

好消息：GPT-6 Astra 正式发布，能力飙升，电脑操作能力断档领先！

坏消息：目前只向组织客户开放，甚至连 Pro20×都没资格使用。。。我特喵的！！！😡只能先看一些社区爆料信息解解瘾！

上下文 1.05M，最大输出长度 128K， 价格方面直接和 Fable5.1 打平，每百万输入 10 美金，输出 50 美金。

最让我感到兴奋的是 Astra 直接操作电脑的能力，也就是 Computer use 的成功率得到巨额提升，而且速度快了一倍！

去操作 Word、剪映、AE、PS、 测试软件、读取控制台报错……可以说，以后可能不需要各大软件开放 API，Astra 直接像人类一样操作就完事了！对法律、剪辑等领域的影响显著。。。

还有一个在 Codex 里面很惊艳的一点，Astra 的主观判断性加强，可以边问边做！

如果涉及到需要用户补充信息，他会弹出一个问题窗口，自己还在干一些不需要补充信息的任务，不会像之前一样就傻傻等着。

在长任务上也很爽！以前自动压缩可能会把之前的一些要求压缩没了，如果不加深度链接，也不会跨窗口搜索信息。

但现在它会主动跨窗口查找相关信息，也可以搜索更早的工具输出，目前在 config.toml 主动打开，未来几周会变成默认选项。

🚨2024 年中美 AI 圈最轰动的一个案子，终于判了。

2024 年 3 月 6 日，美国警方在加州 Newark 抓捕了 38 岁的前 Google 工程师Linwei Ding。

当时这个新闻非常大。

美国司法部指控他在 Google 工作期间，盗取了大量与 AI 超级计算机有关的商业机密，包括 TPU、GPU、SmartNIC，以及如何把成千上万张芯片组织成 AI 超算集群的软件系统。

最初的起诉是 4 项商业秘密盗窃罪，每项最高可以判 10 年。

然后大家才发现，这哥们背后的故事比“Google 工程师偷文件”精彩得多。

严格来说，他甚至不是从 Google 离职以后才回国创业。

2022 年，他还在 Google 上班的时候，就已经开始和国内 AI 公司接触。

到了 2023 年，他直接创办了上海至算科技，自己担任 CEO，做的正好就是他最擅长的东西：大规模 AI 算力集群管理。

至算后来还进了XX创坛，签了协议，用 7% 股份换取投资，并在 2023 年 11 月参加了投资人路演。

我当时对这个项目印象非常深。

因为他的路演材料吹得相当狠：

做过 Google 万卡级算力平台，全球真正有能力搭建这种系统的人没有几个。

至算内部的材料说得甚至更直接：

他们有 Google 万卡平台的经验，接下来只需要“复制、升级”，再做一个适合中国的算力平台。

结果也恰恰是这场路演，把他暴露了。

2023 年 12 月，Google 发现自己的员工居然正在北京以“至算科技 CEO”的身份参加创业路演，于是开始倒查他的内部记录。

这一查，就查出了从 2022 年开始持续了一年多的文件上传记录。

检方后来称，他把 Google 的内部源码先复制进 Apple Notes，转成 PDF，再上传到自己的个人 Google Cloud，以绕过公司的数据防泄漏系统。后来案件扩大，涉及超过 1000 个文件、2000 多页 Google AI 机密资料。

当年这个案子刚爆出来的时候，国内基本没什么公开讨论空间。

我们那段时间甚至被明确告知不要聊、不要吃瓜。

所以当时虽然很多 AI 圈的人都知道这个事情，但真正公开写的人其实非常少。

两年过去，现在终于有结果了。

今年 1 月，陪审团一度判他 7 项经济间谍罪和 7 项商业秘密盗窃罪全部成立。

本来看到这里，我都以为这哥们可能真的要进去很多年了。

🚨2024 年中美 AI 圈最轰动的一个案子，终于判了。

2024 年 3 月 6 日，美国警方在加州 Newark 抓捕了 38 岁的前 Google 工程师Linwei Ding。

当时这个新闻非常大。

美国司法部指控他在 Google 工作期间，盗取了大量与 AI 超级计算机有关的商业机密，包括 TPU、GPU、SmartNIC，以及如何把成千上万张芯片组织成 AI 超算集群的软件系统。

最初的起诉是 4 项商业秘密盗窃罪，每项最高可以判 10 年。

然后大家才发现，这哥们背后的故事比“Google 工程师偷文件”精彩得多。

严格来说，他甚至不是从 Google 离职以后才回国创业。

2022 年，他还在 Google 上班的时候，就已经开始和国内 AI 公司接触。

到了 2023 年，他直接创办了上海至算科技，自己担任 CEO，做的正好就是他最擅长的东西：大规模 AI 算力集群管理。

至算后来还进了XX创坛，签了协议，用 7% 股份换取投资，并在 2023 年 11 月参加了投资人路演。

我当时对这个项目印象非常深。

因为他的路演材料吹得相当狠：

做过 Google 万卡级算力平台，全球真正有能力搭建这种系统的人没有几个。

至算内部的材料说得甚至更直接：

他们有 Google 万卡平台的经验，接下来只需要“复制、升级”，再做一个适合中国的算力平台。

结果也恰恰是这场路演，把他暴露了。

2023 年 12 月，Google 发现自己的员工居然正在北京以“至算科技 CEO”的身份参加创业路演，于是开始倒查他的内部记录。

这一查，就查出了从 2022 年开始持续了一年多的文件上传记录。

检方后来称，他把 Google 的内部源码先复制进 Apple Notes，转成 PDF，再上传到自己的个人 Google Cloud，以绕过公司的数据防泄漏系统。后来案件扩大，涉及超过 1000 个文件、2000 多页 Google AI 机密资料。

当年这个案子刚爆出来的时候，国内基本没什么公开讨论空间。

我们那段时间甚至被明确告知不要聊、不要吃瓜。

所以当时虽然很多 AI 圈的人都知道这个事情，但真正公开写的人其实非常少。

两年过去，现在终于有结果了。

最后只留下商业秘密盗窃罪。

9 月 1 日正式宣判：12 个月减 1 天监禁。

探索了几天 Fable 5.1，按宝玉老师的思路调了一遍，终于摸到它的最佳用法：

Effort 设 Medium（别开 Max，额度会 ×1.5）

默认模型用 Fable 5.1新开一个 Agent Session，只在第一条提示词末尾加一句：Fable 5.1 只负责思考和规划，具体任务交给 sub agent with Opus 5

效果很不错，Claude 总额度和 Fable 总额度按固定比例一起消耗，当前Session后续调研、执行则会自动派给 Opus 5 Sub Agent。

quotedTweet.text:
基本上你只要让 Fable 指挥其他 Agent 干活，这两个进度条就能持平。

大部分任务你选 Fable + High（或者Medium，千万别Max及以上），然后后面加一句：
> 注意你的主要任务是分析、编排和验证，具体任务尽可能交给 subagent（Opus 或 Sonnet）去执行。自己只做需求澄清、方案拆解、任务分发和结果验收，实现类工作（读大量代码、写代码、跑测试、批量修改）一律用 Agent 工具派给 subagent 执行。

text:
I tested GPT-Astra on mathematics. It's a quantum leap. You can talk with the model and prove the statements live in Lean. The feeling is absolutely stunning. You can verify your ideas, compile truth. For a mathematician it feels like finally we arrived in the era where we can focus entirely on the ideation and exploration. Each lemma flows once the logic is set. Before the verification was lagging behind but Astra is very fast and for many tasks the formalization happens as you write your argument in Codex. 

If you tell the model to use literate programming + LaTeX you end up with your proof combined with the Lean code, everything explained as you wrote, mixed with small chunks of Lean which are digestible. 

I don't want to go back to the era where the only confirmation of the proof was "aha". Now the "aha" is followed by a green tick that indeed tells you that you have captured the essence. Imagine how cool it will be to have all the lemmas of the world combined in one giant database, pointing to people and models who found them. You compose and mix your ideas and build on the shoulders of the giants. But you see much further now and build much faster. And we are just at the beginning of those changes. So much work to do, so much fun!

quotedTweet.text:
GPT-6 Astra is here! This is a big moment for our research team - years of work on pretraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training have come together in our most capable and aligned model yet. It can build and test software, work across apps on your computer, and even help you take a crack at open scientific problems!

Capabilities that felt like grand challenges a few years ago have become tools people can actually use. One example is Computer Use - if you’ve tried this before and felt like it was too slow or not good enough, I encourage you to give it another shot. We’ve come a long way since Operator, and it “just works” now.

We’re also asking these systems to act on your behalf for more consequential work. Agents needs to stay aligned with your goals and values, think transparently, and respond to oversight even when tasks become difficult. We’ve made substantial progress on these behaviors in Astra, alongside stronger monitoring that can stop potentially unauthorized actions. That work is part of what makes this release possible.

I think alignment is one of the most important research frontiers in AI, and it remains far from solved. Our ability to understand and align models has to keep pace with model capabilities. We want to give people more room to think, build, and discover with increasingly powerful tools that remain *under their control*.

Huge thanks to the researchers and teams who got us here. There’s a lot more work ahead, and I’m incredibly excited about what we can make possible in the near future!

text:
Truly tragic story of a young boy who was murdered in Philadelphia in front of Bobby and his kids in 2020.

67% of major cities already had ALPR/Flock programs in 2020 (when COVID was happening), but Philadelphia did not start theirs until 2024. 

This murder went unsolved.

quotedTweet.text:
And here’s the *strongest* case for Flock 

In November 2020, we lived in downtown Philly in Rittenhouse Square. After dinner, I took all 3 kids (and our dog) to the Christmas Village at City Hall. To give my wife a break, I took all of them by myself.

As we reached the (former) Santander Bank, I saw a car drive up and stop about 20 yards in front of us. The driver got out, walked over to a young boy/man sitting on a bike and shot him in the face. The boy fell over by some potted plants, and then the man leaned over him and continued to shoot him. Point blank. 

The shooter then got back in his car and drove away, towards us.

My kids, thank God, had no clue what happened other than very loud bangs and yelling. I told my son, who was 6, to run home as fast as he could. I had my 4 and 2 year in the double stroller and I pushed it as fast as I could. Running awkwardly with the leash on my wrist.

As I ran down the street back, the shooters car went past us and then turned  10 feet in front of us down a side street, called Ranstead. I pulled out my phone and tried to get a photo of the car. Instead I just got a blurry picture of my son running for his life with car lights in the background

The boy who was killed, across from City Hall mind you, was 20 years old. He had recently testified against some criminals on another murder he had witnessed.

To this day, his murder is unsolved.

Had Flock been monitoring license plates, it seems very reasonable that instead of this grainy useless picture, the police would have had much better chance of catching them.

result.text:
And here’s the *strongest* case for Flock 

In November 2020, we lived in downtown Philly in Rittenhouse Square. After dinner, I took all 3 kids (and our dog) to the Christmas Village at City Hall. To give my wife a break, I took all of them by myself.

As we reached the (former) Santander Bank, I saw a car drive up and stop about 20 yards in front of us. The driver got out, walked over to a young boy/man sitting on a bike and shot him in the face. The boy fell over by some potted plants, and then the man leaned over him and continued to shoot him. Point blank. 

The shooter then got back in his car and drove away, towards us.

My kids, thank God, had no clue what happened other than very loud bangs and yelling. I told my son, who was 6, to run home as fast as he could. I had my 4 and 2 year in the double stroller and I pushed it as fast as I could. Running awkwardly with the leash on my wrist.

As I ran down the street back, the shooters car went past us and then turned  10 feet in front of us down a side street, called Ranstead. I pulled out my phone and tried to get a photo of the car. Instead I just got a blurry picture of my son running for his life with car lights in the background

The boy who was killed, across from City Hall mind you, was 20 years old. He had recently testified against some criminals on another murder he had witnessed.

To this day, his murder is unsolved.

Had Flock been monitoring license plates, it seems very reasonable that instead of this grainy useless picture, the police would have had much better chance of catching them.

Sooooooo honored to be on their team.

As for the mysterious $250 donation from some random billionaire to my child’s Trump Account, perhaps before composing dramatic theories about my financial circumstances, you could try mastering the fundamentals of reading and comprehension.

I suggest starting with the word “citizen.” Then perhaps move on to: “What exactly is a Trump Account? Who qualifies for one? And, most importantly, does receiving one mean the recipient has somehow declared financial ruin?”

Once you’ve conquered those concepts, we can move on to the more advanced material.

And finally, your charming declaration that all “Amerikaner” are scammers was a particularly impressive contribution to the discussion. Nothing says serious intellectual argument quite like condemning an entire nationality while simultaneously demonstrating such a heroic misunderstanding of the subject.

I hope this helps, skattebolletjie. 📚

但你要时刻盯着鸡，因为它吃饱了后会随处下蛋。但是当你把鸡圈养起来，它就会只吃米不下蛋。

如果你打开笼子，然后再把米撒出去，它也只会追逐米而去，根本不会在意谁在喂它。所以你不能把手里的米全部撒出去，因为鸡只想要米，当你手里没有米，鸡就会立马离开你。

所以你想吃什么样的鸡肉，取决于你怎么喂米，只要有米，喂的好哪怕是带着鸡仔的老母鸡都会跟随你。@justinsuntron

We gave our AI employee a job we assumed one of us would have to do.

I asked him to build the monitoring stack for the newsroom. I had not touched the setup.

1. Set it up and put the feed in this channel. Every lab, release page and changelog, deduplicated, posting here so nothing arrives twice and nothing is missed.

2. Connected it to the story archive. Read access only for now. It can check what you have already covered, it cannot edit anything.

3. Ran it against last week as a test. He found the stories you actually ran, and a few you had missed. Those are in the thread.

He came back with it done and asked me to approve one thing before it went live. He wants write access and he left that switched off. I approved it. That was my entire involvement.

Covering AI means watching more sources than a person can read in a day.

I was shocked.

What do you use to keep up? We are always looking.

Try free at @viktor_com. $100 in credits, no card. Full link in my first reply.

• From Q1's slow-drip hedging & $UVIX +90% expansion

🚀 [NEW RESEARCH DISPATCH] A Structured Drama of Volatility: Deconstructing the First 8 Months of 2026

If you view the financial markets merely as chaotic price fluctuations, you miss the profound structural beauty governing volatility derivatives. 

Over the past 8 months, the VIX performed a highly structured, almost scripted drama:
• Horizon Mean: 18.53 | Range: 14.25 – 31.04
• The Q1 Creeping Friction ➔ March Monsoon (+90% UVIX spike)
• The April 7 Geopolitical De-escalation ➔ The Snap Back to Contango
• The Asymmetry of Compounding (+60% SVIX V-shaped resurrection)

Here is a quick breakdown of the physics governing the 2026 macro cycle 👇

---

1️⃣ Act I: The Q1 Slow-Drip Hedging & The Coiled Spring
Throughout Jan & Feb, institutions systematically accumulated put options as a geopolitical insurance policy. But because $VXF30 Spreads remained in Contango, every sudden 1-day spike faced heavy roll-decay resistance. Spikes were rapidly erased, compressing the spring until the Feb 28 joint strikes snapped it open.

2️⃣ Act II: The March Monsoon & The Fisherman’s Moment
March locked into full Backwardation ($VXF30 Spread < 0%). For one glorious month, Long VIX ETFs experienced legendary expansion (2x $UVIX skyrocketed ~90% to peak at 217.20; 1.5x $UVXY hit 61.85). The fisherman speared the monster. Meanwhile, unhedged -1x $SVIX plummeted -30% into the March floor.

3️⃣ Act III: The April 7 Catalyst — Geopolitics Flips the Weather Engine
The violent inflection on April 7 was driven by the single most powerful geopolitical reset of the year: Trump announced the pause/de-escalation of military operations in Iran after-market. VIX M1 futures collapsed -10.7% (24.98 ➔ 22.15) in hours, violently snapping the curve back into Contango for the first time in weeks.

4️⃣ Act IV: The Asymmetry of Compounding ("Water Dripping Through Stone")
Between April and September, VIX fell from 21 to 14.5. Counterintuitively, the thickest profits for Short VIX ETFs did NOT occur during the instant VIX collapsed, but through the daily, compounding carry—small percentage gains multiplying against an ever-expanding capital base. Both $SVXY and $SVIX executed massive V-shaped resurrections to stand net profitable YTD.

Conversely, $UVIX evaporated by -70%—a decay so aggressive it defies standard mathematical intuition.

---

--> **pray for common sense spending**:  your agent shouldn't violate regional laws; pray that your agent spends the money on what it's supposed to spend it on
--> **pray that it makes the right choice when it can't make all choices**:  your agent(s) should *economize* -- i.e., makes the *right* choice on what to pay for when it can't pay for everything it selects as candidate purchases

Pay-and-pray = playing around

Global financial system can't run on infra that is only safe enough for fun & games.

text:
How to post-train a model to personalize it on your code repo? In our latest research in Bespoke Labs, we post-trained a model to improve its performance on a given Github repository. 

Starting from Inkling base,  we use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with trajectories coming from a strong teacher model, and reinforcement learning (GRPO) on repository-specialized environments that we curated. SFT gave a 52pp improvement in performance on the held-out fontTools evaluation set. Further RL training lifts the total improvement to 57pp compared to the base Inkling model.

In addition to the in-distribution evaluation our post-trained Inkling shows good performance on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Lite while becoming 40% more token efficient due to post-training. 

Read our full research blog post here:
https://t.co/i9Xj0siSRb

Many thanks to Thinking Machines Lab for their credit contribution that helped support this research.

LDS Testimony from someone who does not consider themselves LDS

For close to twenty years I had not gone to church. Not, at least, to any church or any place with the intention of fully committing to it. I had thought about God for most of those years. I had read and argued and wondered. What I had not done was commit.

I was working from home the day my dad walked into the room and told me that Charlie Kirk had been killed.

My son was one year old.

The first thing I felt was disbelief. The second, close behind it, was sorrow. Not the sorrow of politics. I did not agree with Charlie Kirk on every ideological point, and that was never the source of it.

It was an overwhelming sadness about the kind of world my son was inheriting. A young father had been murdered in public for holding opinions that some people did not share. My son was one. His world had just shown him what it does to young fathers, and he was too small to know it, and I was not.

Then it got worse. In Los Angeles, people were rejoicing. Some of my coworkers were glad. Most were indifferent. Between the gladness and the shrug I went into something I can only call existential shock. Whatever you thought of the man, a husband and a father had been killed for speaking, and the people around me were either pleased or unbothered. Hatred at least still cares about what it hates. Indifference to a public murder has stopped caring about anything at all.

That was the day the word darkness stopped being a metaphor for me. It is easy to say the world is dark. We say it flippantly and poetically, the way we say the sky is gray. I mean something more literal than that. I came to believe, and I still believe, that there is a spiritual war being waged over this world. Darkness is not only the absence of light. It is a thing with an appetite, and it takes many forms. Political violence is one of its forms. So is the crowd that cheers it. So is the shrug.

I was in a headspin. I was processing all of this and very emotional, and so I did what a person does when the floor gives way. I went looking for the sacred. I went to three churches.

I went back to Mass first, because that is where I came from. No one mentioned what had happened. No one spoke of anything that was going on in the world. There was a guitar. It might as well have been an evangelical service, and for a Mass that is a strange thing to be able to say. I did not feel anything of the Spirit there. So I went to an evangelical service, and once again nothing of substance was given. Nothing reached down to where I actually was.

I do not say this to condemn either congregation. I say it because it is part of the story. I had come in from a world that had just shown me its face, and I found churches that seemed to be looking at the same screens as everyone else, flattened the same way, offering the same comforts on the same terms.

A church that has learned to sound like the culture has very little to say on the day the culture reveals what it is. I had come looking for something that stood outside the world and could speak to it. I did not find it in the first two places I looked.

Then I went to the Latter Day Saint ward in Manhattan Beach.

In that tradition the blessing of the sacrament bread is entrusted to young men, often still in their teens, and the prayer they say is fixed. The words must be spoken exactly. If a word is missed, the prayer is said again from the beginning.

On that morning the young priest at the table was a boy with a cognitive disability and a severe speech impediment. He stood over the bread and he struggled to get the words out. He labored through that prayer syllable by syllable, and the whole room waited on him, and nobody hurried him.

I sat there and tears came down my face. I had tears because it was so beautiful.

I want to try to say what happened, because it matters for everything that follows. When you feel that the world is filled with darkness, and then in a single moment the world becomes a far more beautiful place than you had thought it could be, something has entered the room. I felt light coming into that room. Not a mood. Not a sentiment.

An arrival.

The people who came before us, in every age and every culture, would have known what to call it. The holy is not something you reason your way toward. It is something that comes upon you. It undoes you and it draws you, both at once. You tremble and you cannot look away. I was doing both.

Catholics believe in the real presence of Jesus Christ. We believe that in the bread Christ is made manifest, truly and substantially, not as a symbol but as himself. I know that many Latter Day Saints do not share that belief, and that is okay. I am not going to pretend the two traditions say the same thing about what happens on that table.

But I will tell you what I saw. That boy, with every ounce of his being, and I mean being in its fullest sense, the whole of what he was, was showing reverence and prayer to his Lord. He was blessing the bread so that the people could partake of the bread of Jesus Christ. And in that act, real presence was being made manifest. I believe that to be true.

But it was not only that. What broke me open was who the boy was, and where he was standing.

Outside that room, in the secular world, he is the kind of person a great many people dismiss. Maybe he gets bullied at school. Maybe he is talked over, or talked around, or treated as an obstacle to the schedule. Every other institution I know of would have found him something else to do, something out of the way.

And here he was the center of the room. Every eye was on him. He had been given the most important words that would be spoken that morning, and he had been given the time to speak them. He held an elevated status, and everyone present was content to wait on him.

I stopped and thought about how beautiful that was, and I have not stopped thinking about it since. Here was a disabled child, and he was the one blessing the bread. It was one of the most beautiful things I had seen in a church in decades.

And I could not help holding the two images side by side. The world had just silenced a fluent man in the middle of a sentence, and a crowd had cheered. The kingdom had just handed its holiest words to a boy who could hardly form them, and a room full of people had bowed their heads and waited. That is the difference between the two kingdoms. That is the whole difference.

All of this leads me to the point I actually want to make.

When it comes to arriving, or arriving again, at religious truth, we make a catastrophic error. It is the characteristic error of secular thought and of the postmodern mind, and most of us absorbed it without ever choosing it. We assume that everything must be treated like the scientific method. We assume that faith is a kind of equation, that you prove it the way you prove a theorem, by reason and logic and evidence lined up in the correct order, and that if you cannot do that you are not entitled to believe.

Nothing in the human story supports the assumption. For as long as there have been human beings, since we came down out of the trees, religious truth has not been arrived at by proof.

It has been arrived at by encounter.

Our ancestors buried their dead and carved ornaments tens of thousands of years before anyone wrote a word.

They met the sacred before they argued about it. They stood in front of something and knew they were being addressed.

That is where religion begins, in every people and in every age, and it is still where it begins. The modern person has been trained to be immune to being addressed, to stand behind a pane of glass and evaluate. But the glass is the anomaly. The encounter is the norm.

Truth, in the religious sense, is an encounter with the sacred. It always has been and it always will be.

Truth happens at the LDS Church on Sundays.  This I know.

how I view the truth & the Book of Mormon

In all of human history, from any anthropological standpoint you care to take, no people ever came to the truth of their religion by rational empiricism. The idea would have been unintelligible to them. 

Truth was found in ritual. It was found in story, in the sacred meal and the sacred place, in the burning bush and the still small voice. Truth is the encounter with the sacred. It is not something you get by reading a nice book by philosophy and concluding, after due reflection, that it contains a nice idea. 

We have fallen into the habit of treating religious truth as though it belonged in the same category as scientific truth. It never did. It was never meant to.

Religious truth is the truth of a sunset. It is the truth of looking into your baby's eyes for the first time. It is the truth of a toddler grabbing your hand and dragging you across the room to show you his toy. It is the truth of looking at the love of your life across an altar and knowing you are sealed for eternity. It is sitting next to the new widow at church on the first Sunday she comes alone. That is truth. That is the truth of Scripture. That is the truth Jesus speaks of when He says He is the way, the truth, and the life. He does not say He is a correct proposition. He says He is a Person you can come to.

Nowhere is all of this clearer than in the Book of Mormon, and nowhere is the category mistake more common. We spend enormous energy arguing about the book in the descriptive register. Geography. Metallurgy. Genetics. What the archaeologists have and have not found. Critics attack on that ground and defenders rush to hold it. Much of that work is honest and some of it is valuable. But the book itself never proposed to be known that way, and it says so on nearly every page.

Ultimately, the Book of Mormon is an invitation. Come unto Christ, and be perfected in Him. 

Everything else is commentary.
